Bobrowniki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bobrowniki, Poland

Not demolished. In 1854, the village of Irena was founded near a new military fortress in Dęblin, and many of Bobrowniki's Jews relocated there for the economic opportunity it offered; by 1939, only about 300 Jews remained in Bobrowniki itself, compared to roughly 3,300 in Dęblin and Irena. During the Holocaust, Germans killed about 300 Jews directly in this cemetery and buried them in a mass grave here; Jews from the Dęblin Ghetto were later transported to the Sobibór and Treblinka death camps. Established in 1744, this cemetery also served the Jews of Dęblin and Irena, who had none of their own. Completely destroyed during and after WWII, it was renovated between 1983 and 1984 through the efforts of Bobrowniki-born Jisrael Ignacy Bubis, who erected two memorials — one to the Holocaust victims at the mass grave site, and a second in memory of his own mother.
